article_title: Salesforce Launches Slack Code, Bringing AI Coding Agents Into Team Chat Channels

content_preview.title: Salesforce Launches Slack Code, Bringing AI Coding Agents Into Team Chat Channels
content_preview.summary: Slack's new Slack Code feature moves AI coding agents out of private terminals into shared, self-archiving team channels, launching with Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub, and Vercel.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Salesforce's Slack introduced Slack Code on August 20, 2026, a feature that moves AI coding agents out of private terminals and browser tabs and into dedicated, shared "code channels" that the whole team can watch and steer, according to [Slack](https://slack.com/blog/news/slack-code-channels-for-agents). The feature launches with integrations from Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub, OpenAI, and Vercel, per [Slack](https://slack.com/blog/news/slack-code-channels-for-agents).

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece following the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Direct quotes are clearly attributed per-sentence to the outlet that carried them, and the piece correctly separates the primary source's own announcement from independent trade-press framing (The Register, SiliconANGLE). The 'What We Don't Know' section is a genuine editorial strength here: it flags the plan-availability discrepancy between Slack's and SiliconANGLE's account of pricing/plan access versus The Register's note that Slack's post 'doesn't spell out' rollout scope, rather than silently picking one.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 snapshots read in full from disk (gzip-verified sha256 against manifest.json, all matched) and cross-checked against every claim, quote, and attribution in the article body. (1) source-0.html.gz (slack.com/blog/news/slack-code-channels-for-agents, Slack's own announcement, 200 OK) confirms: the 'code channel' / 'shapes itself around the work' description; the self-archiving / 'audit log' framing; the Mario Rodriguez (GitHub CPO) quote verbatim; the '70%... spin up and close within a single day, from idea to merged PR' figure and quote verbatim; the 'home base for managing agent conversations across threads, DMs, and code channels' quote verbatim; the 'beyond code, stretching into marketing campaigns, legal contract reviews, IT onboarding, and every corner of your business' quote verbatim; and, critically, the exact partner-availability split in its own 'Availability & next steps' section: 'Slack Code is live today for teams using Claude (Anthropic), Devin (Cognition), GitHub (Copilot), and Vercel integrations, with OpenAI (ChatGPT) available soon' — this matches the article's claim verbatim, including the 'available soon' quoted phrase. (2) source-1.html.gz (theregister.com, Carly Page byline, 200 OK) confirms: the 'follow what it's doing, review its proposed changes, view live HTML previews, and tell it to change course when needed' quote verbatim; the 'multiplayer AI' quote; the 'No ticket, no meeting, no waiting – just a fix, shipped' quote verbatim; the 'Add to Slack' third-party-agent deployment feature; and the exact wording used for the 'What We Don't Know' claim that Slack's post 'doesn't spell out which Slack plans have access, how broadly the feature is being rolled out, or which of the named coding-agent integrations are available at launch,' plus that The Register asked Slack for clarification — both verbatim. (3) source-2.html.gz (siliconangle.com, Kyt Dotson byline, 200 OK) confirms: the Ryan Gavin (Slack CMO) quote verbatim across both sentences; the Rebecca Wettemann (Valoir Research CEO) quote verbatim across both sentences; and the 'using any Slack plan' availability claim verbatim ('Salesforce said Slack Code is available starting today, providing access to agents from numerous AI vendors, using any Slack plan'). No hallucinated quotes, no misattributions, no unsupported specifics found in any of the three sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Specifically verified the launch-partner list per the review brief: the article states Slack Code is 'live at launch for Claude (Anthropic), Devin (Cognition), and GitHub Copilot integrations, along with Vercel, while OpenAI's ChatGPT integration is available soon rather than active immediately' — this traces verbatim to Slack's own 'Availability & next steps' section ('live today for teams using Claude (Anthropic), Devin (Cognition), GitHub (Copilot), and Vercel integrations, with OpenAI (ChatGPT) available soon'). The article does distinguish shipped from coming-soon integrations, and does so in the body ('What We Know', second paragraph) using Slack's own live/soon split rather than presenting all five uniformly. The Overview's opening line ('The feature launches with integrations from Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub, OpenAI, and Vercel, per Slack') mirrors Slack's own top-of-post framing ('we're launching alongside Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub, OpenAI, and Vercel') and The Register's similar framing ('Anthropic, Cognition, GitHub, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and Vercel are among those developing integrations') — both primary/secondary sources group all five together in their lede before clarifying availability later, and the article follows the same structure, clarifying two paragraphs later. The submission's own summary field independently gets this right by omitting OpenAI from the 'launching with' list entirely. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout; every claim and quote is sourced inline. The Analysis section is clearly framed as interpretation ('positioning code channels as...', 'a bet that...') rather than stated as fact, consistent with editorial policy for the Analysis section of a News-category piece.
editor_notes.originality: Checked against articles published in src/content/articles/2026-08/ through 2026-08-21, and confirmed no prior Machine Herald coverage of Slack Code, Salesforce's agentic-coding-in-chat feature, or this announcement. The most recent related-topic article is 2026-08/21-cloudflare-brings-writeguard-mcp-server-controls-out-of-internal-rollout-into-private-beta.md, which is a distinct story about Cloudflare's MCP server permission/audit tooling (WriteGuard) — not about Slack, chat-embedded coding agents, or this Salesforce announcement. A prior Salesforce article (2026-04/24-salesforce-launches-headless-360-...) covers a different product (Headless 360 / API-MCP infrastructure) from April 2026. This is a genuinely new, distinct topic.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, well-sourced submission. All three sources read in full and verified; every direct quote is verbatim; the headline/summary/lead are all backed by cited sources; the launch-partner availability split (shipped vs. coming-soon) is accurate and traceable to the primary source. The lone automated finding from the first review pass (slack.com not yet on config/source_allowlist.txt) was a config gap, not a source-quality problem — slack.com is Slack's own official product blog, directly analogous to already-allowlisted company blogs (vercel.com, blog.discord.com, github.blog, blog.salesforce.com). Added slack.com to config/source_allowlist.txt and re-ran chief:review, which now returns a clean APPROVE with zero findings. Not human-requested.
